No — the underlying form is Turkish, not Arabic.
Sevinc can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Turkish-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Sevinc, sevinc. Script forms are سوينچ, سوینچ, سَفِينْج, सेविंच.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
